posts.excerpt: Alicia’s Deals may receive a small commission via affiliate links in this post. Please see my full disclosure here.
posts.text:
Alicia’s Deals may receive a small commission via affiliate links in this post. Please see my full disclosure here.
Prime Day is officially right around the corner (October 6-7), but you do not have to wait until next month to score the best perks. The early deals are officially live, and this year, Amazon dropped a massive surprise for book lovers and music fans alike.
Right now, Prime members can head over to this Amazon Page to score four months of Amazon Music Unlimited completely free (non-Prime members can still grab a fantastic three-month free trial!).
My absolute favorite part? Audible is now included directly inside the Amazon Music Unlimited app! That means you get a free best-selling audiobook credit every single month of your trial.
If you grabbed the free Audible deal I posted back in June, this offer actually stacks—giving you an extra four months of free access! Just make sure to cancel your original standalone Audible trial so you don’t duplicate accounts. Amazon Music Unlimited auto-renews at $11.99/month after the trial, but you can easily cancel anytime with a few clicks in your Amazon settings.
🎧 How to Claim This Deal (Don't Miss This Step!)
Because this is a brand-new setup, a few readers have gotten turned down by searching the wrong app. Follow these quick steps to ensure it works flawlessly:
Click this link: Lock in your free months via the Amazon Music Portal.
Download the app: Make sure you download and open the Amazon Music App (not the regular Audible app).
Claim your book: Navigate to your music dashboard, go to the Audible tab, pick your audiobook, and start listening!
What I’ve Listened to So Far:
Listening to books during my daily drive has happily turned my car into a mobile library. I am officially hooked on listening during my morning routines, workouts, road trips, flights, and errands around town. If you are wondering how to spend your first free monthly credits, here are the titles I've tried:
Audiobook | Genre | Listen Time | Perfect For
The Calamity Club | Historical Fiction | 28h 44m | Long road trips & family sagas
Yesteryear | Satirical Thriller | 11h 15m | Pop-culture fans & drama
Biological War | Investigative Non-Fiction | 13h 10m | Thriller & current events fans
Atomic Habits | Self-Improvement | 5h 35m | Quick, life-changing upgrades
The Mini Reviews
The Calamity Club by Kathryn Stockett
The Vibe: From the bestselling author of The Help, this is a captivating novel about family, friendship, resilience, and fierce women.
My Take: The narration is top-notch. At nearly 29 hours long, this single audiobook will cover your carpool commutes for the next month (and you'll never get bored)!
Yesteryear: A GMA Book Club Pick by Caro Clare Burke
The Vibe: A viral "tradwife" social media influencer wakes up trapped in the brutal, unglamorous reality of 1855. Part psychological thriller, part dark comedy satire.
My Take: This is the bingeable Good Morning America Book Club pick everyone is talking about—grab your copy before the upcoming Anne Hathaway movie hits screens. I honestly could not stand the main character, Natalie, but somehow that made the book even better!
Biological War: A Scenario by Annie Jacobson
The Vibe: An instant New York Times bestseller exploring a ticking-clock roadmap following the accidental release or outbreak of a biological agent.
My Take: The depth of research in this book is genuinely frightening. It is the perfect follow-up if you read her smash-hit Nuclear War: A Scenario. It definitely leaves a lasting impression!
Atomic Habits by James Clear
The Vibe: The ultimate guide to breaking bad routines and letting tiny 1% daily changes compound into massive results over time.
My Take: Investing in yourself doesn’t have to cost a dime (especially when you can listen to this book for free). If you haven’t read this yet, you’re missing out on small, actionable life hacks that deliver massive results. It worked for me years ago, and those daily systems are here to stay!
🎯 Next on My List...
I just downloaded the new release, Whistler: A Novel by Ann Patchett, and will report back when I finish it.
What are you listening to in the car lately? Are you team Fiction (give me a great story!) or
team Non-Fiction (make me smarter during my commute)?
Drop your favorite audiobook recommendations in the comments below so I can add them to my upcoming queue!
Enjoy!

posts.title: Mark Your Calendar for National Park Service Fee-Free Days in 2025!
posts.excerpt: We are so lucky to have 22 national parks in AZ! It's one of my goals to see as many of the national parks around the country as possible!
posts.text:
We are so lucky to have 22 national parks in AZ! It's one of my goals to see as many of the national parks around the country as possible!
If you plan your trip well, you can avoid paying admission fees!
"The 2025 free entrance days are:
January 20 – Martin Luther King, Jr. Day
April 19 – First Day of National Park Week
June 19 – Juneteenth National Independence Day
August 4 – Great American Outdoors Act Signing Day
September 27 – National Public Lands Day
November 11 – Veterans Day
How to plan a national park trip
Where:
With over 400 national parks, monuments, and historic sites, there’s something for everyone. Visit NPS.gov/findapark to explore the park options nearest you. If you’re visiting a park that normally charges an entrance fee, review your entrance pass options before you arrive.
When:
The National Park Service is waiving the entrance fee for parks on six days in 2025, so consider planning your visit then. Otherwise, pick a date that works for you to visit and keeping in mind seasonal changes, how much daylight you’ll need, and if you need to get to the park early in the day to get parking or take advantage of lower temperatures.
How:
Some national parks require advanced reservations for camping, lodging, or timed entry. Research and book early to secure your spot, especially for popular parks.
Pick the right activity for you:
Review the possible activities, including ranger-led programs, scenic hikes, tours, and more. Planning allows you to maximize your experience while balancing active days with relaxation. Consider your experience and skill level when picking your activity.
Prepare for the unexpected:
Sometimes, our travel plans might change last minute or even during the hike. Do your research to know what else the park has to offer if you don’t end up being able to do what you planned that day. For example, if there’s more rain than you prepared for, visit the park museum or take a scenic drive. Make sure you check the park website or the NPS App for updated conditions, seasonal closures, and alerts.
Bring the right gear:
Plan like a Park Ranger and pack essentials like water, appropriate clothing, and maps. You can download park maps for offline use from the NPS App so you can find your way even if there’s no Wi-Fi. Note that water might be hard to come by in some parks, so make sure you bring your own, especially if you’ll be outside for a while.
Most parks are free to enter all of the time, approximately 100 out of 430+ national parks charge an entrance fee. With at least one national park in every state, no one is too far from an adventure. Take a look at www.nps.gov/findapark to see what adventure awaits and refer to our Trip Planning Guide as you prepare for your next visit. Mark your calendars and get ready for a year of adventure in 2025! "
Check out one of my favorite Christmas gifts from this year here...it's a game that celebrates the national parks (and makes me more curious to see more of them)!
Enjoy!

MathMagicians has a dedicated mentor, teachers helping them design the FUN curriculum, and a team of volunteers who are ready to share their love of math with the kids. There will be games, prizes, snacks, and lots of fun and learning for everyone in attendance! They are "on a mission to make learning fun and enjoyable for young kids by teaching them math through fun and interactive activities."
I was helping out at the camp checking kids in and out (full disclosure Kaitlyn is my daughter and Karina is her lovely friend) and one mom told me that her daughter did not want to go at first but came away saying it was the "best thing ever". Another mom said her son couldn't wait to get home and call his aunt to demonstrate his new division skills. The feedback was incredibly positive and the kids left saying they liked math more at the end of the week than they had at the beginning of the week.
Head over here to follow MathMagicians on Instagram!
Enjoy!

posts.title: The Maricopa County Summer Reading Program is BACK!
posts.excerpt: I have always been a huge fan of the Maricopa County summer reading program and I'm happy to report it is not a casualty of Covid-19! Pre-readers, kids, teens,…
posts.text:
I have always been a huge fan of the Maricopa County summer reading program and I'm happy to report it is not a casualty of Covid-19! Pre-readers, kids, teens, and adults can head over here to join and start logging reading minutes.
You'll be able to pick up prizes in August at your local libraries!
"Maricopa County Reads is the award-winning summer reading program provided by the Maricopa County Library District to all public, tribal and military base libraries within Maricopa County. The primary goal of the program is to interrupt the summer slide, the common term given to the learning loss experienced by children while transitioning between school years. The secondary aim of the program is to promote early literacy among pre-readers and their families during the summer months.
Several approaches are employed to accomplish these goals:
Interrupt the Summer Slide
Keep kids reading every day so they will not lose the reading comprehension skills that they learned during the school year.
Read for 20 minutes a day! Reading 20 minutes a day will help build a lifelong habit of reading.
Kids and adults can both count the minutes when adults read to children or kids read to adults!
Advance Early Literacy Skills
Conduct early literacy education programs for children and their caregivers.
Encourage teens and adults to read with children and model independent reading behaviors.
Encourage caregivers to engage in early literacy activities with children.
Build Home Libraries
Read for 20 minutes a day, every day over the summer and earn a free book!
Free books are available for all ages, from babies to adults.
You can donate your book to a child if you do not want to keep it.
Emphasize the Fun of Reading
Attend fun, literacy-based events at the library to earn digital badges and gain points towards your goal of unlocking a free book!
Have fun interacting with the online program by completing challenges and earning digital badges.
Connect Readers with Community Experiences
Visit a community partner to learn something new and earn secret codes to unlock badges and earn more points.
Try a community experience to connect your kids with books in a more meaningful way by bringing things to life that they have only read about.
The Maricopa County Reads online summer reading program began in the summer of 2013. It has continued to grow, and now hosts all 67 public, tribal and military base libraries within Maricopa County. More than 80,000 children, teens, and adults participate in the program annually."
Enjoy!

"The featured exhibits at the museum are the Putnam Collection Center, Lowell’s Lunar Legacy, and the Rotunda Museum.
Daily tours and nighttime telescope viewing are included
Children under 5 enter for free
Children aged 5-17 enter for $4-$8; depending on day
Hours of business are Monday – Saturday from 10 a.m. – 10 p.m. and Sundays 10 a.m. – 5 p.m.

Promotional value expires 120 days after purchase. Amount paid never expires. Limit 1 per person, may buy 1 additional as gift(s). Limit 1 per visit. Must use promotional value in 1 visit(s). Merchant is solely responsible to purchasers for the care and quality of the advertised goods and services.
About Lowell Observatory
Lowell Observatory was established in 1894 by Percival Lowell atop a mesa overlooking downtown Flagstaff, Arizona. In 1960, a dark-sky research site was established at Anderson Mesa, 10 miles southeast of Flagstaff. Today, the 180-acre use permit area on the Coconino National Forest hosts several telescopes and the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer. In 1994, in celebration of the centennial year, the Steele Visitor Center was opened. As of 2015, well over a million people have passed through its doors. Some 100,000 visitors each year enjoy tours, telescope viewing, exhibits, multimedia shows, and more. Percival Lowell inspired millions with his tireless advocacy of astronomy in the public eye, and his observatory continue this commitment today.
In 2012, Lowell Observatory embarked on its greatest adventure yet with the completion of the 4.3-meter Discovery Channel Telescope (DCT). This new facility, in full science operations as of 2015, vastly expands the breadth of research capabilities for Lowell astronomers and those of its institutional partners. Even more exciting, partnership with Discovery Communications provides an avenue to bring research results and breathtaking images to hundreds of millions worldwide. In December of 2017, Lowell Observatory announced a major expansion to the Mars Hill Campus that included an Open Deck Observatory, Universe Theatre, and Open Sky Planetarium.
The Giovale Open Deck Observatory is expected to ‘break ground’ in Summer of 2018. Our Mission The mission of Lowell Observatory is to pursue the study of astronomy, especially the study of our solar system and its evolution; to conduct pure research in astronomical phenomena; and to maintain quality public education and outreach programs to bring the results of astronomical research to the general public.
Lowell Observatory

Head to the Children’s Museum of Phoenix where everyone will get in free from 5-9 PM. Tickets are usually $11 each, so this is quite an opportunity to play for less!
Still have energy? Go to the Phoenix Art Museum for their First Friday event. Everyone will get in for free from 6-10 PM (tickets are usually $15 for adults, $6 for kids).
If it’s date night, you might want to think about checking out the Arizona Science Center. Adults 18 and over will get in for free (general admission). Head over here for more information and to check out the lecture series.
Visit the Heard Museum for their First Friday Native + You program.Everyone will get into the museum FOR FREE from 6-10 (tickets are usually $18 for adults, $7.50 for kids).
Enjoy and have fun!

posts.title: Thinking of Buying a New Car Over Labor Day Weekend? Five Deals Edmunds Says Are Great!
posts.excerpt: If you're thinking about buying a new car this Labor Day weekend, start here with Edmunds and get quotes online from dealerships all over town (when you have…
posts.text:
If you're thinking about buying a new car this Labor Day weekend, start here with Edmunds and get quotes online from dealerships all over town (when you have people fighting over you it's always a good thing). You'll have a number before you even leave the house, no tense negotiations required.
It's a great time to save on the 2015 models as the 2016s are coming. Here are some deals that Edmunds says are especially good:
"2015 BMW 3 Series
For those looking to enter the luxury market, discounts on this entry vehicle may be an attractive offer. The 3 Series includes sedan and hatchback models, and scores four out of five in J.D. Power ratings for overall quality. However, the 3 Series scores three out of five, or “about average” for predicted reliability.
In some regions, the 3 Series is already being sold for more than $1,500 below its true market value, or the Edmunds.com-calculated standard price customers pay based on past sales, which starts at about $32,950 for the gas engine sedan. The site expects BMW dealers to advertise cash rebates, lease specials and low-interest financing for end-of-summer deals on the 2015 model.
2015 Chevrolet Volt
Chevy’s GM, +1.05% take on the plug-in hybrid is slated for a major redesign later this year, which means big discounts are on the horizon for the 2015 model. Low gas prices this year have stifled demand for the environmentally friendly vehicle, so prices will be especially reduced. Reed says hybrids continue to see a decline in demand due to standard engines becoming more fuel efficient.
“There are some really good non-hybrid options now that have come up over the last five or six years,” Reed says. “They’ve stolen some thunder from hybrids.”
Edmunds.com estimates that most current offers on the 2015 Volt are already $4,000 below its true market value. Though the model scored four out five for predicted reliability in the J.D. Power ratings, its overall quality score was just two out of five, suggesting it may not be the best bang for your buck. The MSRP on the Volt is $34,345.
2015 Honda Civic
This highly rated model may be seeing discounts up to $2,000 below its true market value, according to Edmunds.com. The Honda Civic HMC, +1.59% sedan has an A rating from the site, and scores five out of five for overall quality and predicted reliability in J.D. Power ratings. Despite the high marks, the Civic rates about average for overall performance and design.
Reed says the Civic is one of the more popular models he was surprised to see on the list of Labor Day discounts, making this deal especially “attractive.”
The 2015 Honda Civic Hybrid’s manufacturer’s suggested retail price starts at $24,735.
2015 Toyota Prius
Suffering from the same gas price-induced stagnation as the Chevrolet Volt, dealers are cutting Toyota PriusTM, +2.37% prices down as much as $3,000 below true market value to stimulate demand, says Edmunds.com. Toyota is also offering an additional 0% financing for 60 months to qualified buyers to sweeten the deal. The MSRP on the Prius is $24,200.
Reed attributes the deep discount to the upcoming redesign for the 2016 model. The Prius has not been redesigned since 2004, giving it a relatively outdated body design. If you aren’t picky about looks, however, the offers on the 2015 model are a great way to save money.
“For people that are concerned about saving money, these cars are perfect for them,” Reed says.
Though the Prius scores low for overall quality and overall performance and design, it holds a perfect score for predicted reliability in the J.D. Power ratings.
2015 Volkswagen Passat
While Volkswagen isn’t implementing a total redesign of the midsize sedan for 2016, Edmunds.com estimates that the planned mid-cycle refresh is pushing prices down by $1,000 below true market value, in addition to cash incentives and 0% financing.
MSRP for the Passat starts at $21,340, however it has relatively average ratings, scoring three out of five for overall quality and two out of five for predicted reliability in the J.D. Power ratings."
Thanks Market Watch!

posts.title: Just in Time for Spring Break...Pogo Passes Good at a NEW VENUE!
posts.excerpt: Spring Break is next week for many Arizona kids and just in time Pogo Pass secured a new fantastic venue! You can still head over here to get a pass for just…
posts.text:
Spring Break is next week for many Arizona kids and just in time Pogo Pass secured a new fantastic venue! You can still head over here to get a pass for just $39.98 with code ALICIA (usually around $100).
To make the deal even more exciting, if you buy or renew a pass in March (remember to use code ALICIA) you'll be automatically entered to win 4 tickets to Wicked at Gammage!
Starting March 6th, your pass will get you into Makutu's Island in Chandler twice with your year-long pass (Monday-Friday). Tickets are usually $10 each and here's a description of the place:
"Makutu’s (Ma-coo-two’s) Island, one of America’s largest indoor play places, is a trip into fantasy and adventure for children of all ages and a perfect way to beat the Arizona heat. Designed with a tropical theme, Makutu’s is a lush, exciting indoor “island” with towering trees, climbs, bungee, zip tracker, arcade, café, theater, toddler zone and mysterious caves.
The centerpiece of Makutu’s Island is its magnificent indoor tree. Filled with tunnels, tubes, mole-holes, fire-poles and slides, the magnificent tree offers hours of fun and adventure. Around the tree’s perimeter, guests will find animals carved within its extensive roots and a comical three-animal totem pole. Within the majestic tree, the “banana” slide is a sure thrill as it starts on the forth level in the air and winds more than 35 feet around the outside of the tree to its base.
After exploring the tree, many of Makutu’s guests find themselves in one of the three adjoining play structures including the Blue Fantasy Tree, Pirates Cove and Palm Slide. Less rigorous than the old oak tree, these areas are perfect for the less-experienced island traveler and include tunnels, caves and a zip-line.
In addition to Makutu’s main four play areas, the island also offers its smaller guests a special toddlers area. Oscar’s Lagoon is a slower placed environment of Makutu’s smallest “castaways.” In the Lagoon, toddlers will enjoy three small slides and soft foam blocks."
The POGO Pass will help your family have the ultimate spring break "staycation". Check out what else your pass includes:
Castles and Coasters: Each Pogo Pass holder recieves one (1) visit to Castles~n~Coasters for a *Silver Pass (worth $29.99). This includes unlimited rides and mini golf.
Each Pogo Pass holder receives general admission to the Phoenix Zoo two (2) times. To gain admission to the Zoo, simply present your Pogo Pass at the admission window. Some experiences require an additional fee. Admission to ZooLights and select special events is not included. An adult general admission is usually $20, so this is a $40 value for adults. There is a new baby orangutan that I can’t wait to visit! Head over here to see more adorable pics (or better yet grab your Pogo Pass and visit in person).
Sunsplash: Each pass holder can attend Golfland Sunsplash one (1) time. Your pass is good for one (1) SunSplash General admission ticket. Simply present your Pogo pass at Sunsplash Guest Service window to be scanned to obtain waterpark wristband. Sunsplash is closed for the season but since your pass is good for a FULL YEAR, you can use this next summer. A general admission ticket for adults is usually $29.99.
IDEA museum (used to be Arizona Museum for Youth): Each pass holder can attend i.d.e.a Museum Two (2) times during normal business hours (closed on Monday). Children 1 yrs of age and up are $8 admission if they do not have a valid Pogo Pass. Children are required to wear socks in play area. ** Excludes opening weekend (Fri, Sat, Sun) of opening exhibitions, 3 weekends a year. Simply present your Pogo Pass at admissions desk for entrance. Since admission is usually $8, this adds $16 of value to your POGO pass.
Enchanted Island: Your Pogo Pass is good for a Day Pass four (4) times at Enchanted Island Park Friday and Sundays during regular business hours. Not valid during Enchanted Island special events (I would call ahead before you go). Limited capacity, first come first serve. Some rides may require additional charge. A day pass is usually $17 for anyone under 54 inches, $10 for anyone over.
Sun Devil Athletics: Pogo Pass is a accepted for general admission tickets to ALL of the following ASU athletic home games: Women’s Basketball, Soccer, Wrestling, Volleyball, Gymnastics, Track and Field. **No need to pre-register for tickets to attend. Simply present your Pogo pass at will call or the front gate to gain admissions.
Arizona Diamondbacks: One (1) ticket per game per pass holder for two (2) home games at Chase Field for the MLB Regular Season. Game options for this season will come out soon.
National Comedy Theater: Each pass holder can attend 2 shows. Please call for a reservation. Seating is limited. First come first serve. Note: Please honor your reservations. Reservations will be cancelled for those who are not in their seats 5 minutes prior to show. Tickets are usually $14 each.
Skateland: Each pass holder can attend Skateland two (2) times per month. Skateland has three (3) different locations available to pass holders. Simply present your Pogo Pass card at the front counter to gain admission to Skateland. Skate Rental not included. There are 3 locations (one in Mesa, one in Glendale, and one in Chandler).
Phoenix Rock Gym: Pogo Pass holders can attend Phoenix Rock Gym two (2) times. Simply present your Pogo Pass at the front counter to gain admission to Phoenix Rock Gym. Waiver required for 18 and younger. Limited capacity, first come first serve. *Climbing gear available upon request for $5.
Jump Street: Each Pass holder can attend Phoenix Jump Street two (2) times. Pass is good for a one (1) hour jump session each attendance. NOTE: This one is only available during normal business hours Mondays and Wednesdays.
Stratum Laser Tag: Pass holders can attend stratum two (2) times. Each pass holder receives one (1) complimentary game of laser tag each time they attend. Pass is valid for 12 months. NOTE: Pogo Passes may be used on Mondays and Wednesdays 4:30-close. Pogo Passes may not be used during school holiday breaks or Stratum’s designated holiday hours. No exceptions.
Tempe Paintball: Pogo Pass holders can attend Tempe Paintball one (1) time per month for 12 months that include gun rental, air, and 100 paintballs. Check for seasonal hours and scheduled groups or events before scheduling your visit. Keep in mind that all participants must be 10 years or older, and must sign a waiver before prior to entering the arena. Note: This is not good on Saturdays.
Arizona Rattlers: (1) One ticket per game per pass holder for three (3) Arizona Rattlers home games at the US Airways Center for the AFL regular season. There will be select games posted before the next regular season.
Fat Cats is coming to Gilbert soon and will be part of the POGO Pass (including bowling)!
Enjoy your passes and please note that venues are subject to change!

posts.title: HOT! Buy or Renew a Pogo Pass This Weekend and Get a $5 Target Gift Card! Still Just $39.98!!!
posts.excerpt: This is SUPER HOT! Head over here to buy a Pogo Pass for just $39.98 with code ALICIA and you'll get a $5 Target gift card with every purchase THIS WEEKEND…
posts.text:
This is SUPER HOT! Head over here to buy a Pogo Pass for just $39.98 with code ALICIA and you'll get a $5 Target gift card with every purchase THIS WEEKEND ONLY! This really is the BEST VALUE OUT THERE and you can buy them as gifts! The year won't start until the receiver activates their pass. So many of us have WAY TOO MUCH STUFF and this is giving an entire year of memories! :-) Make sure you pick the gift card option! You'll get your Target gift card in 48 hours!
I thought I’d type out a full list of when and where your Pogo Pass is good. I am constantly hearing from readers that the Pogo Pass is their favorite Alicia’s Deal of all time. Venues can change but this is the best value around. I like this so much more than buying a membership to one place, you can enjoy places all over town!
Castles and Coasters: Each Pogo Pass holder recieves one (1) visit to Castles~n~Coasters for a *Silver Pass (worth $29.99). This includes unlimited rides and mini golf.
Each Pogo Pass holder receives general admission to the Phoenix Zoo two (2) times. To gain admission to the Zoo, simply present your Pogo Pass at the admission window. Some experiences require an additional fee. Admission to ZooLights and select special events is not included. An adult general admission is usually $20, so this is a $40 value for adults. There is a new baby orangutan that I can’t wait to visit! Head over here to see more adorable pics (or better yet grab your Pogo Pass and visit in person).
Sunsplash: Each pass holder can attend Golfland Sunsplash one (1) time. Your pass is good for one (1) SunSplash General admission ticket. Simply present your Pogo pass at Sunsplash Guest Service window to be scanned to obtain waterpark wristband. Sunsplash is closed for the season but since your pass is good for a FULL YEAR, you can use this next summer. A general admission ticket for adults is usually $29.99.
IDEA museum (used to be Arizona Museum for Youth): Each pass holder can attend i.d.e.a Museum Two (2) times during normal business hours. Children 1 yrs of age and up are $8 admission if they do not have a valid Pogo Pass. Children are required to wear socks in play area. ** Excludes opening weekend (Fri, Sat, Sun) of opening exhibitions, 3 weekends a year. Simply present your Pogo Pass at admissions desk for entrance. Since admission is usually $8, this adds $16 of value to your POGO pass.
Enchanted Island: Your Pogo Pass is good for a Day Pass four (4) times at Enchanted Island Park Friday and Sundays during regular business hours. Not valid during Enchanted Island special events (I would call ahead before you go). Limited capacity, first come first serve. Some rides may require additional charge. A day pass is usually $17 for anyone under 54 inches, $10 for anyone over.
Sun Devil Athletics: Pogo Pass is a accepted for general admission tickets to ALL of the following ASU athletic home games: Women’s Basketball, Soccer, Wrestling, Volleyball, Gymnastics, Track and Field. **No need to pre-register for tickets to attend. Simply present your Pogo pass at will call or the front gate to gain admissions.
Brunswick Bowling: A YEAR OF FREE BOWLING! - 2 Free games per week for 52 weeks! *Shoe Rental not included. Saturdays/Some Holidays/Special events are excluded & reservations are not accepted. For groups of 10+, please call ahead to check lane availability.
Arizona Diamondbacks: One (1) ticket per game per pass holder for two (2) home games at Chase Field for the MLB Regular Season. Game options will come out before the next regular season (that has to be better than this one was).
National Comedy Theater: Each pass holder can attend Three (3) shows. Please call for a reservation. Seating is limited. First come first serve. Note: Please honor your reservations. Reservations will be cancelled for those who are not in their seats 5 minutes prior to show. Tickets are usually $14 each.
Skateland: Each pass holder can attend Skateland two (2) times per month. Skateland has three (3) different locations available to pass holders. Simply present your Pogo Pass card at the front counter to gain admission to Skateland. Skate Rental not included. There are 3 locations (one in Mesa, one in Glendale, and one in Chandler).
Phoenix Rock Gym: Pogo Pass holders can attend Phoenix Rock Gym two (2) times. Simply present your Pogo Pass at the front counter to gain admission to Phoenix Rock Gym. Waiver required for 18 and younger. Limited capacity, first come first serve. *Climbing gear available upon request for $5.
Jump Street: Each Pass holder can attend Phoenix Jump Street two (2) times. Pass is good for a one (1) hour jump session each attendance. NOTE: This one is only available during normal business hours Mondays and Wednesdays.
Stratum Laser Tag: Pass holders can attend stratum two (2) times. Each pass holder receives one (1) complimentary game of laser tag each time they attend. Pass is valid for 12 months. NOTE: Pogo Passes may be used on Mondays and Wednesdays 4:30-close. Pogo Passes may not be used during school holiday breaks or Stratum’s designated holiday hours. No exceptions.
Tempe Paintball: Pogo Pass holders can attend Tempe Paintball one (1) time per month for 12 months that include gun rental, air, and 100 paintballs. Check for seasonal hours and scheduled groups or events before scheduling your visit. Keep in mind that all participants must be 10 years or older, and must sign a waiver before prior to entering the arena. Note: This is not good on Saturdays.
Arizona Rattlers: (1) One ticket per game per pass holder for three (3) Arizona Rattlers home games at the US Airways Center for the AFL regular season. There will be select games posted before the next regular season.

If you have some pounds to lose (whether 5 or 100), you may want to check out this new program by Nutrisystem. Click here to get a free one-week trial. If you don't like it, cancel anytime in that week and you're not out anything. If you love it the price starts at $2.69/week (very do-able for most of us).
I lost 30 pounds a couple of years ago and have kept it off so far but it's always hard (and I know the weight could come back very easily). I love programs that make it easy. Watch the video to get more of a sense of how NuMi works. They have loads of recipes that fit your calorie plan (based on what you have at home). The program offers unlimited tips, advice, and support every single day. There are lots of fitness options you can do wherever you are. I love that it gives you tools to succeed. Losing the excess weight helped me feel so much better, I really want to keep it off for life.
Another alternative that worked well for me is My Fitness Pal. Head over here to check it out, it's a free calorie counter that you can take anywhere. You make what you eat public (which does make eating that cookie a little bit less tempting).
If you want to get moving, you can head over here to get a free 3-day pass to any 24 hour Fitness. I'm all for working out for free, but sometimes it's really nice to take a class (especially when it's as hot as it is right now)!
If you have a weight loss tip that has worked for you, I'd love to share it! Dumping Diet Coke and drinking unsweetened green tea instead has done a world of good for me.

posts.title: Get into Big Surf FOR FREE on Friday for Their World's Largest Swim Lesson!
posts.excerpt: If you're not busy early Friday morning, take the kids to Big Surf! They're trying to break their own world record for the largest swim lesson.
posts.text:
If you're not busy early Friday morning, take the kids to Big Surf! They're trying to break their own world record for the largest swim lesson.
"World’s Largest Swimming Lesson – Friday, June 20th!
Once again, Big Surf Waterpark is a host site for The World’s Largest Swim Lesson’s (WLSL) attempt to break the Guinness World Record for largest simultaneous swim lesson. This year, we will defend our own personal Guinness World Record as the hosting the most participants of any host site…we’re hoping to exceed 906 swimmers. Waterparks and pools around the globe will host a swim lesson and water safety class to spread the message that swim lessons can save lives! Admission is free to this event and we ask that everyone arrive no later than 7 a.m."
If you're there for the swim lesson, you can stay the rest of the day for free.
Friday is also First Responder's Day!
"First Responder’s Day – Friday, June 20th!
On the same day we attempt to break a Guinness World Record during the World’s Largest Swimming Lesson, we’d like to offer complimentary admission to all First Responders. This includes police officers, fire fighters, EMT’s, paramedics and emergency room physicians & nurses. A big deserved “Mahalo” to all of you from us!"
Could be a fun, FREE day! It's so much nicer out early anyways!
Enjoy!
Thanks Bargain Believer!
